Definition: , also (before a vowel) οὐκ, and (before an aspirate) οὐχ a primary word; the absolute negative (compare G3361) adverb; no or not:--+ long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, (can-)not, + nothing, + special, un(-worthy), when, + without, + yet but. See also G3364, G3372.
BiblicalUsage: No is the commonest negative in the New Testament, and it does heavy work. Paul says he baptized none of the Corinthians but Crispus and Gaius, and John says God is light and in Him is no darkness at all.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the little word no carries the weight of the whole gospel: God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all, and that is why I can trust Him.
